Information flows unidirectionally from input to output and is well -suited for tasks like image classification and regression.• Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) : These networks use convolutional and pooling layers to extract hierarchical features from input data, making them ideal for processing images and videos.• Recurrent Neural Networks (RNNs) : RNNs have recurrent connections that loop back on themselves, maintaining memory of past inputs. They are suitable for sequential data tasks like time series analysis, natural language processing, and speech recogn ition.• Transformers : These use an attention mechanism to add context to input data and are foundational for most large language models used today.• Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) : GANs consist of a generator and a discriminator engaged in a competitive learning process, useful for generating realistic synthetic images, audio, text, and videos.• LSTM(long -short term memory) v/s GRU(gated recurrent unit) Aspect LSTM(long -short term memory) GRU(gated recurrent unit) Structure LSTMs have three gates (input, forget, and output gates) that control the flow of information. GRUs have two gates (reset and update gates), making them simpler than LSTMs. Complexity More complex due to the additional gates, which allow for better handling of long -term dependencies.Less complex with fewer parameters, which can lead to faster training times. Use case Suitable for tasks requiring long -term memory retention, such as long text sequences.Often used when computational efficiency is important and for tasks with shorter sequences.
